newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian Banca Agricola lifts deposit rate.
newsitem.headline: Romanian Banca Agricola lifts deposit rate.

text.p: Romania's state-run bank Banca Agricola SA said it raised interest rates again, effective Wednesday, to protect depositors against surging inflation and conform to tougher monetary policies.
The bank's sight rates rose to an annual 22 percent, up from a previous 18 percent, Banca Agricola said in a statement.
Its one-month rate gained 25 points to 85 percent. Three- and six-month deposits now pay an annual 80 percent, against a previous 60 and 62 percent, respectively.
Banca Agicola's one-year rate rose 27 points to 85 percent.
The bank raised its deposit rates earlier this month after the central bank started to tighten monetary policy, pushing the one-week refinancing rate to 125.45 percent from 90 percent.
Year-on-year inflation soared to 56.9 percent last year from 27.8 percent in 1995 and is forecast to climb to 97 percent this year, led by the freeing of fuel, electicity and food prices.
